elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 applies to “each Party” and expressly states that the cap is mutual.

elements.element: The first limb of the cap is fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 uses “the fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.”

elements.element: The second limb of the cap is USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 expressly provides a USD 1,000,000 limb.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of the 12-month fees limb and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 21.1 expressly uses “the greater of” the two required limbs.

elements.element: Indirect damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Section 21.2 states that “neither Party” is liable for indirect damages, to the extent legally excludable.

elements.element: Consequential damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Section 21.2 states that “neither Party” is liable for consequential damages, to the extent legally excludable.

elements.element: There is an uncapped carve-out for breach of confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Confidentiality breaches are Excluded Claims under Section 21.3 and are therefore excepted from the cap in Section 21.1.

result.reason: The rendered clause fully implements the preferred cap formula, mutual damages exclusion, all required uncapped carve-outs, and the treatment of Customer payment obligations. Assessed independently, the fallback is not fully satisfied because it specifies a cap of 12 months’ fees, while the rendered cap includes a USD 1,000,000 floor. The redline is otherwise targeted and preserves the existing allocation of risk. Drafting quality is reduced because lowercase, undefined “fees” appears alongside the retained defined term “Fees,” creating avoidable ambiguity about which payments count toward the cap.
